text:
Aisha: heads up — ran a small bakeoff with redwood/llm-x.fp8-awq behind prefix cache + continuous batching. Observed a ~6-8% accuracy drop on our eval set compared to no-cache baseline. Latency improved, but cache hit rate collapsed. Logs:
Aisha: ```
cache_hits: 12
cache_misses: 488
avg_latency_ms: 92
95p_latency_ms: 220
model_variant: fp8-awq
continuous_batching: true
prefix_cache_ttl_s: 300
```

Tom: can you paste the runtime config you used (batch_timeout, max_batch_size, cache_ttl, cache_key_mode)?
Aisha: sure — minimal snippet:
Aisha: ```yaml
model: redwood/llm-x.fp8-awq
continuous_batching: true
batch_timeout_ms: 16
max_batch_size: 64
prefix_cache:
  enabled: true
  ttl_s: 300
  key_mode: float32_hash
  prime_on_miss: false
```

Marta: quick thought — AWQ/FP8 can introduce tiny numeric differences in KV generation. If key_mode uses exact float hashing, quantization noise might change keys and invalidate cache entries (so you get a cold cache but with faster per-token decode). That would explain hit-rate collapse + acc regression.
Sam: also seen a "batch-starvation" pattern: continuous batching holds requests waiting for nearby traffic to form a batch, but if cache miss triggers an expensive priming step (e.g., KV fill/warmup for quantized kernels), the overall latency pipeline changes and can bias eval sampling. Suggest turning on prime_on_miss to populate cache proactively.
Tom: can you run an A/B: continuous_batching true vs false, and prime_on_miss true/false? Also vary cache_ttl small/large. I'll put together a 2x2 matrix.
Aisha: ran a quick 4-run test (eval subset 1k):
Aisha: baseline (no cache): acc=83.6, p95=125ms
Aisha: cache + contbatch (fp8, prime_on_miss=false): acc=77.9, p95=220ms, hits=2.4%
Aisha: cache + no-contbatch (fp8, prime_on_miss=false): acc=82.9, p95=180ms, hits=62%
Aisha: cache + contbatch + prime_on_miss=true: acc=83.1, p95=140ms, hits=59%

Marta: okay that's telling — prime_on_miss greatly helps. My hypothesis: continuous batching without priming causes many first requests to be served by a partly-filled KV cache or different kernel path, producing varied outputs. When you prime_on_miss you ensure consistent KV state for subsequent requests so accuracy recovers.
Tom: we should also test INT8-GPTQ variant to see if key stability differs. If INT8 has stable keys, maybe use INT8 for latency-sensitive routes and FP8 for cost-optimized background jobs.
Sam: operational tweak: set min_batch_size=1 and max_wait_ms=8, and add a small jitter to batch timers to reduce request alignment that causes KV churn. Also consider using a lossy but stable key hash (round floats to 3 decimals before hashing) for prefix cache to be quantization-robust.
Marta: code for stable key idea: ```python
def kv_key(tokens, kv):
    # round activations for stable hashing across quant variants
    rounded = [round(float(x), 3) for x in kv_prefix]
    return sha256(bytes(rounded))
```

Tom: I'll schedule the full matrix: variants = [fp8-awq, int8-gptq]; continuous_batching = [true,false]; prime_on_miss = [true,false]; cache_ttl = [30,300,3600]; eval_size = 5k. CI-bot launching experiment bundle.
CI-bot: launched experiments bundle e-3521 (fp8-awq, cont=true, prime=false) and e-3522 (fp8-awq, cont=false, prime=false). Links: https://ci.redwood/experiments/e-3521
Aisha: quick numbers from first two jobs match local. Will let the 5k runs finish.
Sam: also add metric kv_key_stability: fraction of keys that change between float and quant kernels for same prefix. If > 1% we should avoid byte-exact caching.
Marta: agree — add a monitoring alert for cache_hit_rate < 10% on routes with expected warmup.
Tom: plan: run bakeoff, pick config that preserves >99% of baseline accuracy while keeping p95 under target. If not possible with FP8, fallback to INT8-GPTQ for latency-sensitive endpoints. I'll document results in the model-onboarding sheet.
Aisha: summary for now — root cause looks like key instability + cache priming interactions with continuous batching. Mitigations: prime_on_miss, stable-hash key_mode, reduce batching wait, or choose more stable quant variant. Will post final numbers once 5k runs finish. :thumbsup:
